cells.tense: You are gathering the loose threads into one shape, here, with the pen.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Do one small fair thing that nobody will clock. Then put it down and don't mention it, no note, no tally.
cells.core:
You can hold several threads at once and see how they run together. That's the work here: loose pieces of a situation get gathered into one shape, and the shape holds because you're steady enough to carry it. When it's going well, you read the whole pattern from just inside it, weighing what each part needs, and the weighing settles easily because your own sense of what's fair runs underneath it.

So give that sense one small case to settle where no one is watching. Pick a fair thing to do, do it, and stop there. What makes the pattern trustworthy isn't the cleverness of the gathering — it's the small honest thing inside it that nobody asked you for. That's how the shape you hold stays clean.
cells.sheetLine: Fairness settles easily when nobody is counting.

cells.tense: You will have the whole pattern mapped before it has shown its own shape.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: This week, take one piece of the situation and work it at a pace you could hold for a month. Then leave the rest until it's that piece's turn.
cells.core:
You're assembling the whole picture before it's here, and the picture runs past what's actually on the table. Each loose thread gets fitted into a shape before it has had a chance to show what it is. What's moving is the pace, not the thought: the gathering has started racing its own material, and the shape it lands on keeps getting rebuilt when reality arrives late.

One piece, done at a speed you could keep for a month. Not the whole thing, just the next honest piece, at the rhythm that will still be there in four weeks. Then stop and leave the other threads where they are. The pattern you want is built at the speed of the pieces, not the speed of the worry about them.

cells.tense: You were standing at the edge of the pattern, and you've stayed outside it since.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Once this week, sit with the situation as it already stands and keep it quiet for a few minutes. Nothing to fix, nothing to gather.
cells.core:
The pieces are all in your hands, and the shape they'd make is close — close enough to gather in an ordinary afternoon. Instead you've stayed outside the picture, and the not-arriving has gone quiet on you, so it reads as patience. From out there, a shape you could have assembled sits unassembled, and nothing new comes toward it.

Don't gather it yet. First sit with what you already feel about this, quietly, a few minutes. No sorting, no working it out. What you already feel is in you; sitting near it is what makes it usable. Then the gathering becomes a small next move instead of a long wait.

cells.tense: You are gathering these threads for everyone while saying it is only how things are.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: When something good happens, tell the person nearest to it out loud. Then let it sit, without a qualifier tacked on.
cells.core:
You pull scattered threads together — yours, and other people's too — and you carry the shape without calling it carrying. Go by your account of it and you were just following what's there. The pattern is a reading someone did; the gathering is work someone did. You've stood inside it so long that the made thing looks like terrain.

Before you were assembling patterns, you were someone who shared a good thing with the people it belonged to. So when something good happens, say it out loud to the person who'd want to hear it, plainly. That isn't performed gladness. It's the older move underneath the assembling, and it's yours.

attempts.check: The overreaches: in Too Much I claim co-workers are waiting to be told the shape of a project — the record supports the capacity outrunning its integration, not anyone else's experience; a reader could rightly say the bracing is entirely theirs, unremarked by anyone. In Too Little I say the person is standing just outside the pattern — the record supports past-anchoring of the seat, not that they wait at any particular door. The asks survive a wrong read: none requires anyone's response, money, energy, or a safe person — the four acts are self-contained; the one other-person opening (sharing the good news) makes a person the recipient, allowed not required. The sentence serving the writer over the person: 'The pattern is already gathered.' — it exalts the capacity instead of naming the person's part in it; I've rebuilt Unacknowledged around what the person actually carries.

attempts.check: The overreaches: in Too Much I say the shape keeps needing to be rebuilt when reality arrives late — the record supports the capacity running past its material, not a specific outcome. The sentence serving the writer over the person: the old 'The pattern is already gathered.' — it flatters the capacity; I named the person's part instead.
